newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Rail, truck offers soften.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Rail, truck offers soften.

text.p: Rail and truck basis offers in some U.S. soymeal markets were lower Monday as CBOT soymeal prices continued to march higher, dealers said.
"A lot of people are just waiting to see if this market settles down before they do anything," said one river dealer.
In early trade, all nearby soymeal futures contracts made fresh contract highs. As 1045 CST, May soymeal futures were up $3.10 at $268.80 per ton.
The dropping basis has spurred talk about crushers slowing down. One major Midwest crusher was said to be considering slowing production at all its facilities, dealers said.
"There has been a lot of discussion about it (slowing the crush) because cash crush margins have slipped so far," said one meal dealer.
Flooding in the Ohio River Valley was still hampering rail and barge movement and was said to cause one southeastern crusher to stop production, dealers said.
"We're still water bound," said a river dealer. "We're locked out on rail and on the river."
